classification.difficultyReason: Requires equal-angle calculation and rejection of an impossible placement of the given angle.

content.prompt: One of the angles in an isosceles triangle is $160^{\circ}$. Work out the sizes of the other two angles.

answer.worked:
The $160^{\circ}$ angle is the unequal angle, so let each remaining angle be $x^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+160&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of a triangle)}\\2x&=20\\x&=10\end{align*}$$
The other angles are $10^{\circ}$ and $10^{\circ}$.

children.prompt: Explain why there is only one possible set of answers.

answer.short: $160^{\circ}$ cannot be one of the equal angles because two such angles would already exceed $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked: If $160^{\circ}$ were one of the equal angles, their sum would be $160^{\circ}+160^{\circ}=320^{\circ}$, exceeding the triangle's angle sum of $180^{\circ}$. Therefore $160^{\circ}$ must be the unequal angle, giving only $10^{\circ}$ and $10^{\circ}$.
